docs.title: analint
docs.text:
Declare how a system behaves in Python, then check its consistency.

Describe state with entities, transitions with actions, and relationships with invariants. Run concrete scenarios or explore the reachable states to find a counterexample you did not think to write as a test.

pip install analint
analint check path/to/spec/

Requires Python 3.12 or newer. This guide covers analint 0.0.4, including fixed initial worlds, scope keys, explicit initial presence and check --cache. The site tracks the repository's main branch; future unreleased features will be marked explicitly. For development:

git clone https://github.com/angru/analint
cd analint
uv sync --frozen
uv run analint check examples/cloak/

docs.title: Start with a small model
docs.text:
The first-spec tutorial builds a ticket workflow with three reachable states. You will check a successful transition, an intentionally blocked transition, a complete journey and a reachability property, then introduce a defect and read its counterexample.

Your next step Read Understand what a PASS proves Verification concepts Look up a declaration or semantic rule DSL reference Run checks, inspect a model or read JSON CLI reference Give a coding agent the workflow or connect MCP For AI agents Learn from a larger working model Examples gallery

docs.title: What the checker establishes
docs.text:
analint checks the model you declare: its state domains, actions, guards and initial states. A complete exploration can prove safety and reachability within that model. It does not verify that application code implements the specification, and NoDeadEnd establishes that a goal remains reachable rather than that every execution eventually reaches it.

Results distinguish PASS, FAIL and INCONCLUSIVE. A budget-exhausted check cannot silently become a pass. Individual properties can also be NOT_CHECKED when they could not be evaluated. See verdicts and completeness before using the checker as a CI gate.

The project is an early public release; pin a version if you depend on its API. Development and release history live in the roadmap and changelog.

docs.title: For AI agents
docs.text:
analint is built for coding agents as first-class users: every command speaks JSON with a versioned schema, and the model is inspectable without reading source. There are two ways to give an agent that surface.

This page documents the repository's main branch. cache is available since 0.0.3; the other listed MCP operations are available since 0.0.2. The CLI reference covers terminal options, which are not identical to the MCP argument set.

docs.title: Agent Skill (recommended)
docs.text:
The repository ships a portable Agent Skill at skills/analint/. A skill is a plain SKILL.md that teaches an agent when and how to use analint: the show → affects → what-if → apply → check loop, fail-closed verdict interpretation, and the DSL's semantic rules (effects are simultaneous facts, where to put Field/Invariant/Lifecycle, Scope/Param/presence, the loader contract). It carries no scripts — the CLI already owns execution.

SKILL.md is an open format read natively by Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot; Antigravity and other agents that scan a skills/ directory pick it up the same way.

Install — copy the skill into the agent's skills directory:

# Claude Code: project-local or global
cp -r skills/analint .claude/skills/analint
# or  ~/.claude/skills/analint

# Codex / Antigravity: into that agent's skills directory

The agent also needs analint on PATH:

pip install analint        # or: uv add analint

Then drive it in plain language — "use analint to check this spec before editing" — and the skill supplies the workflow.

docs.title: MCP server (optional)
docs.text:
For clients that prefer typed tool discovery over a shell, the same core is exposed as an MCP server with five tools — check, show, affects, explore, trace:

pip install "analint[mcp]"   # then configure `analint-mcp` in the client

Use MCP when the client benefits from discoverable, typed operations or has no normal shell; otherwise the CLI plus the skill is the lighter path.

Configure a local stdio server in your client's MCP settings with executable analint-mcp and no arguments. The process must have access to the spec files and its required Python imports. The exact settings-file format belongs to the client. Paths are resolved on the machine running the server; use absolute paths when the client's working directory is uncertain.

docs.title: Tool reference
docs.text:
All five tools return structured dictionaries. Optional arguments and defaults below match the server's tool definitions.

Tool Required arguments Optional arguments check None path=".", what_if=null, max_states=null, slice=true, tlc=false, cache=false (cache since 0.0.3) show None path=".", kind=null, name=null affects target path="." explore None path=".", query=null, what_if=null, include_graph=false, max_graph_states=null trace A property id in query for a useful request path=".", query="", what_if=null, slice=true

check runs the full validation pipeline. max_states overrides every exploration budget and must be positive; slice=false corresponds to CLI --no-slice. tlc=true tries the supported TLC fallback for INCONCLUSIVE properties. MCP currently exposes no strict, scenario/tag filtering or tlc_timeout parameter; use the CLI when those options are needed.

show returns an overview without a kind, an id list with just a kind, and details with a kind/name pair. Detailed kinds are entity, event, invariant, action, lifecycle, flow, scenario and contract. affects accepts a field, entity/event name or action id.

explore follows the whole model for canonical or query-specific roots. It returns a compact artifact by default. To request the graph, supply both include_graph=true and max_graph_states=N; the latter caps output, not exploration. Above that graph size, the response retains the summary and explains why graph is null. Read completeness separately.

trace accepts an invariant id as well as a query id, despite the argument's name. It follows the same slice and budget decisions as check. A property without a witness returns witness: null with an explanation.

For example, send these arguments to check:

{
  "path": "/absolute/path/to/ticket_spec",
  "max_states": 10000,
  "slice": true
}

Then inspect the witness by passing this to trace:

{
  "path": "/absolute/path/to/ticket_spec",
  "query": "can_archive"
}

docs.title: Workflow and verdicts
docs.text:
1. show the inventory, then inspect the relevant action or contract.
  2. Use affects before changing a field or transition.
  3. Test a proposed property through check(what_if=...) using the same packaged entity imports as the model.
  4. Apply the accepted change and list its behaviour on Spec or Contract.
  5. Run check again and read the overall verdict and per-property findings.

The check response uses analint.check/v1. Treat only verdict: "PASS" and passed: true as success; FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE and individual NOT_CHECKED results require interpretation. Scenarios passing does not establish canonical invariants. A retrieved trace is diagnostic evidence, not a substitute for the full report. See verification concepts.

docs.title: JSON schema identifiers
docs.text:
Response Schema Validation report analint.check/v1 Model inventory analint.overview/v1 Detailed object or id list analint.show/v1 Impact analysis analint.affects/v1 Exploration artifact analint.exploration/v1 Witness/counterexample analint.trace/v1 Operation error, where supported analint.error/v1

Inspect error fields as well as schemas. Some lookup errors retain the operation's schema. Invariant traces identify the property with invariant instead of query; clients should accept both forms.

docs.title: Which to use
docs.text:
Layer Job analint CLI / library the executable source of truth Agent Skill teaches an agent when and how to use analint MCP server typed, discoverable operations with structured results

The skill and the JSON schemas are versioned (analint.check/v1, analint.show/v1, analint.exploration/v1, …) so an agent can detect stale instructions. Validation is always mandatory: a skill is prompt text, not a typed guarantee.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: The examples below use the tutorial model. Replace . with a directory containing spec.py or the path to an entry-point Python file. Run analint --help or analint COMMAND --help for installed-version options.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
analint check .
analint .                         # shorthand
analint check . --format json
analint check . --strict

Checks loading and structure, scenarios, flows, canonical invariants and queries. The overall verdict includes all of these stages.

Option Meaning -f, --format terminal\|json Select human-readable or JSON output -s, --scenario ID Filter scenarios by id; repeat for multiple ids -t, --tag TAG Filter scenarios by tag; repeat for multiple tags --strict Warnings fail the run --what-if FILE.py Merge hypothesis objects for this invocation --max-states N Override canonical and query budgets with a positive integer --no-slice Use whole-model exploration instead of property slices --tlc Hand supported INCONCLUSIVE properties to TLC --tlc-timeout SECONDS Timeout per exported TLC check, at least 1 second; default unlimited --cache Since 0.0.3: persist/reuse explorations of unchanged slices

Scenario/tag filters select scenario execution; they do not turn the command into a scenario-only validation that skips invariants, flows or queries.

The cache directory defaults to ~/.cache/analint; set ANALINT_CACHE_DIR to override it. Caching does not change findings or completeness. Timings measure performed work, so a reused exploration is cheaper than a fresh one.

docs.title: JSON reports
docs.text:
check --format json returns analint.check/v1. Read verdict and passed before inspecting individual results. passed is true only for an effective PASS, including the effect of --strict.

Field Contents spec Root id and name load_errors, structural Load problems and structural findings scenarios, flows Example/journey results and findings invariants, queries Per-property status, state count, trace and findings exploration Findings encountered while exploring transitions summary Aggregated counts, including inconclusive and unchecked invariants

Property results can include slice, elapsed_ms and backend: "tlc". elapsed_ms measures incremental work for that property; shared exploration is charged to its first consumer, and invariant retries are included. Model preparation and shared action coverage are excluded. Summing these timings does not give total command time.

docs.title: show
docs.text:
analint show -p .
analint show action -p .
analint show action resolve -p .
analint show entity Ticket -p .
analint show lifecycle Ticket.status -p .

show [KIND] [NAME] --path PATH always returns JSON. Without arguments it returns the analint.overview/v1 model inventory. With a kind it lists ids; with a kind and name it returns details using analint.show/v1.

Detailed kinds are entity, event, invariant, action, lifecycle, flow, scenario and contract. Query ids are available in the overview or show query; use trace QUERY_ID for a property's witness.

docs.title: affects
docs.text:
analint affects Queue.open_tickets -p .
analint affects Ticket -p .
analint affects resolve -p .

affects TARGET --path PATH returns analint.affects/v1. Targets are fields (Entity.field), entity/event names or action ids. Inspect readers, writers, constraints and scenario coverage before changing the model.

docs.title: trace
docs.text:
analint trace can_archive -p .
analint trace can_archive -p . --format json
analint trace resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket -p .

trace PROPERTY_ID --path PATH returns a query witness or invariant counterexample with state changes. Options are --format terminal|json, --what-if FILE.py and --no-slice.

JSON uses analint.trace/v1, with query or invariant identifying the property, its status, the root, steps and final_state. A property without a witness returns witness: null and an explanation. The command follows check's slice and budget decisions; use --no-slice for the whole model. Adjust the model's budget for a larger trace exploration; trace has no --max-states option.

Successful trace retrieval is an inspection operation. Its process exit code does not replace the property's status or a check verdict.

docs.title: explore
docs.text:
analint explore .
analint explore . --format json
analint explore . --query can_archive --format json --include-graph

explore [PATH] explores the whole model, starting from canonical roots or the roots of --query ID. It accepts --what-if FILE.py and --format terminal|json. --include-graph includes the nodes and edges in JSON; the default is a compact summary.

The analint.exploration/v1 artifact includes source, completeness, summary, findings and graph. graph: null can mean output was intentionally omitted; it does not by itself mean the exploration was incomplete. Read completeness separately. The artifact's content-derived node/edge ids are stable across equivalent runs.

Like trace, explore is an inspection operation; use check as the CI verdict gate. Explore does not have the check command's --max-states, --cache, --tlc or --no-slice switches.

docs.title: Hypothesis workflow
docs.text:
Use the same shared entity classes in your hypothesis and spec. Packaged models use qualified imports, as shown in the tutorial.

analint show -p path/to/spec
analint affects Entity.field -p path/to/spec
analint check path/to/spec --what-if hypothesis.py --format json
# Apply the accepted change to the spec, then check again.
analint check path/to/spec --strict

--what-if merges objects without editing the entry point or permanently changing its cached root. After applying a hypothesis, list new behaviour on Spec or an imported Contract; normal module imports do not register it.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
The following table applies to check:

Code Meaning 0 Effective PASS 1 FAIL: findings, failed scenarios/flows/properties, or strict warnings 2 CLI usage error, such as an invalid option or format 3 Spec failed to load or no root spec was found 4 INCONCLUSIVE, including an unchecked invariant preventing PASS

For show, affects, trace and explore, a successful response means the inspection operation ran; inspect the returned data to interpret verification results. Machine-readable operation errors use analint.error/v1 where supported.

docs.title: CI and local development
docs.text:
For an installed release, gate your spec with:

analint check path/to/spec --strict --format json

Pin the analint version and retain both the exit code and report. Do not turn code 4 into success without an explicit policy for unresolved properties.

From a repository checkout, the documentation is checked with:

uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_documentation.py \
  tests/test_fixed_initial.py::test_fixed_roots_across_check_explore_and_trace \
  tests/test_keys.py::test_key_verdicts_traces_artifacts_and_cache_agree
uv run --frozen --group docs mkdocs build --strict

The docs workflow performs these checks for pull requests and main-branch pushes before its main-branch-only deployment.

docs.title: Verification concepts
docs.text: A specification is a model of state and transitions. Verification asks what can happen under all enabled action choices from the declared initial states. Results depend on the completeness of that model: an omitted action, guard or domain case can make the model prove a property the real system does not satisfy.

docs.title: Scenarios, flows and exploration
docs.text:
Check Starts from Establishes Scenario Its concrete given snapshot One action accepts or correctly rejects this example Flow Its concrete given snapshot This sequence of actions and checkpoints executes successfully Canonical invariant verification Spec.initial, or defaults Each listed invariant holds throughout reachable states Query Its own initial source, otherwise the canonical roots The reachability or safety property for those roots

A passing scenario covers that example. A passing flow shows one executable journey. Neither establishes that all other action orders are safe; that is what the reachability engine examines.

Scenarios and flows have partial worlds: only supplied entity instances are present, and omitted scoped slots are absent. Canonical exploration starts with entities constructible from defaults and scoped slots present by default. Supply required field values and explicit Absent(ref) snapshots through an initial relation or a query's given when needed. A missing required default can prevent canonical verification even though all scenarios pass.

Since 0.0.4: Scope(..., initially_present=False) opts into absent defaults for canonical/query worlds. Explicit snapshots override the scope policy; each query-owned initial source starts independently from those defaults. Scenario and flow partial worlds keep the same behavior. See the identity and presence example.

docs.title: Initial states and domains
docs.text:
Spec.initial=Initial(vary=[...], where=[...], given=[...]) declares a finite set of canonical roots. vary enumerates field domains; where filters combinations; given fixes other field values or supplies instances without defaults.

Domains can come from booleans, enums, lifecycle states, bounded integer fields or Field(values=[...]). A BoundField in vary expands over its scope. max_candidates limits candidate generation; exceeding it is an error, never a truncated selection of roots.

Since 0.0.4: omit vary (or use vary=[]) for a fixed relation: Initial(given=[...]) builds one candidate from defaults plus those snapshots. where still applies, so a false filter yields an error rather than a vacuous PASS. Initial() selects the defaults-built world. This does not require enumerating finite domains for fields that stay fixed. Versions before 0.0.4 require a non-empty vary. See the fixed-root example.

A query can specify one of given, given_any or initial:

  • given=[...] supplies or overrides instances in the defaults-built root.
  • given_any=[[...], [...]] enumerates admissible roots explicitly.
  • initial=Initial(...) generates them declaratively.

Without its own initial source, a query uses the canonical roots. Multi-root queries must satisfy their requirement for every admissible root; for Reachable, each root must have a path to a matching state. A trace records which root it starts from.

Numeric annotations alone do not bound a domain. An increasing int counter without an upper bound may generate infinitely many distinct states. Use finite abstractions and explicit bounds that reflect the requirement. Ordinary hard bounds reject an out-of-range transition with a finding; saturate=True clamps values at the thresholds and therefore changes the model's meaning.

docs.title: Verdicts and completeness
docs.text:
The command's overall verdict has three values. Individual invariant and query results can additionally report NOT_CHECKED.

Result Meaning Overall consequence PASS The check established its requirement for the model and roots Can contribute to overall PASS FAIL A counterexample, evaluation defect or other failure was found Overall FAIL INCONCLUSIVE The available exploration did not settle the property Prevents overall PASS NOT_CHECKED The property could not be evaluated, for example because no canonical initial state could be built Prevents overall PASS

An existential witness can settle a reachability check before the graph closes; universal safety or unreachability requires sufficient complete coverage. A concrete defect can fail a capped run. A property applicable in zero states cannot silently pass: vacuous queries fail, while an invariant never evaluated is NOT_CHECKED on a complete exploration and INCONCLUSIVE on a capped one.

Automatic invariant verification and scenario checks are distinct. An invariant whose direct entity/slot references are absent from a scenario is skipped there; finite quantifiers instead range over the present members. Empty ForAll is true; empty Min/Max is an evaluation error. Include the required data when using scenarios to exercise a rule.

For check, JSON passed is true only for an effective PASS. --strict makes warnings fail the run. Exit codes are documented in the CLI reference.

docs.title: Transition semantics
docs.text:
All execution paths use one transition kernel. Preconditions and terminal/presence guards can reject an action before effects. Effects apply simultaneously: every right-hand side reads the pre-state. The checker then checks postconditions and state invariants. A state violating an invariant is retained as a counterexample but is not expanded further.

An action cannot modify any field of an entity whose lifecycle is terminal, or delete that terminal entity. Two effects writing the same field are a structural error. Reading or modifying an absent scoped instance is rejected.

Expect.FAIL passes only for an intended pre-execution rejection. An effect error, failed postcondition or failed then assertion is still a failed scenario. Events are materialized observations; emission does not automatically dispatch another action. Exploration excludes actions requiring external event payloads and reports them as unassessed rather than falsely declaring them dead.

docs.title: Slices, budgets and repeated checks
docs.text:
By default, check explores each invariant or query on its cone of influence: the state it reads, the actions that can affect it, and the dependencies of those actions. Independent processes need not pay for their full Cartesian product. JSON records the slice. check --no-slice uses the whole model instead.

Spec.max_states bounds canonical invariant exploration; queries have their own max_states. check --max-states N overrides all budgets for that invocation. An exhausted budget preserves INCONCLUSIVE. Raising the budget can help a large finite model, but cannot close an unbounded domain.

trace follows the property exploration used by check; trace --no-slice selects the whole-model path. explore always explores the whole model for its chosen roots. Sliced traces keep out-of-slice fields at their root values. One documented difference is that whole-model NoDeadEnd counts a state illegal under an out-of-slice invariant as a dead end, while that slice does not; the invariant violation still fails the run in its own check.

Since 0.0.3: check --cache persists explorations by a digest of the slice, roots, budget and engine source. An unchanged slice can reuse work across runs; model changes invalidate the relevant entries. The cache returns the same semantic findings as a fresh run. Check timing can change because it measures work actually performed, and shared work is charged to its first consumer.

docs.title: TLC fallback
docs.text:
check --tlc hands supported properties left INCONCLUSIVE to TLC on the same slice. It requires Java and a TLC jar, selected by ANALINT_TLC_JAR or a discovered Quint/Apalache installation. Use --tlc-timeout SECONDS to bound each exported check. A result decided by TLC carries backend: "tlc".

The exporter mirrors the transition kernel and refuses constructs it cannot represent. Unsupported exports and timeouts leave the property INCONCLUSIVE. Current fallback supports invariants and Reachable, Unreachable and AlwaysHolds; NoDeadEnd and DeadActions are not exported. Floats, Min/Max and unsafe absent-slot reads are examples of export restrictions. TLC is an additional verifier for the same finite abstraction; it does not turn an unbounded or incomplete model into a proven system.

docs.title: Recoverability and scope boundaries
docs.text:
NoDeadEnd(goal=...) asks whether a path to the goal exists from every reachable state. A system can satisfy this while repeatedly choosing a loop and never finishing. The query establishes recoverability, not liveness, fairness or termination of every execution.

analint does not model scheduling fairness, real time, probabilities, unbounded collections, automatic event delivery or concurrency inside one action. Model finite state alternatives explicitly and keep these assumptions visible. It also does not check that implementation code conforms to the model.

docs.title: DSL reference
docs.text: Import public declarations from analint. The first-spec tutorial is a complete runnable model; snippets below illustrate individual declarations and may refer to names defined there or in the linked examples.

docs.title: State: Entity and Field
docs.text:
Subclass Entity and annotate fields. An instance carries values; a class-level field is an expression used in predicates and effects.

from analint import Entity, Field


class Wallet(Entity):
    balance: int = Field(0, ge=0, le=5)


Wallet(balance=3)       # concrete snapshot
Wallet.balance >= 1    # predicate, evaluated against a state later

Fields without defaults are required in snapshots. Unknown, missing required or constraint-violating values are rejected at construction.

Field option Meaning Field(default, ge=..., gt=..., le=..., lt=...) Numeric constraints, checked on snapshots and transitions Field(default, values=[...]) Explicit finite scalar domain Field(default, ge=..., le=..., saturate=True) Clamp numeric effects at thresholds instead of rejecting an overflow Lifecycle(...) as a field default Initial value, allowed edges and terminal states for a state field

Booleans, enums, lifecycle states, bounded integers and explicit value domains can supply finite choices to Initial. Numeric bounds define the abstraction: use thresholds deliberately, especially with saturation.

docs.title: Predicates and expressions
docs.text:
Comparisons ==, !=, <, <=, > and >= build predicate values. Fields and arithmetic expressions support +, - and *. Name expressions and predicates to reuse them; they are data, not callbacks.

from analint import And, Implies, In, IsNotNull, IsNull, Not, Or

can_pay = And(Wallet.balance >= Order.total, Order.total > 0)
remaining = Wallet.balance - Order.total

Use And(...), Or(...), Not(...) and Implies(a, b), rather than Python and, or, not or chained comparisons. In(field, values), IsNull(field) and IsNotNull(field) cover membership and null checks. Boolean fields can appear directly in predicate positions, such as pre=[Client.active].

docs.title: Invariant
docs.text:
Invariant(predicate, id="", label="") describes a state relationship.

from analint import Implies, Invariant

resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket = Invariant(
    Implies(Ticket.status != Status.NEW, Queue.open_tickets == 0),
    label="Resolving the only ticket clears the queue counter",
)

Listed invariants are automatically verified from the canonical roots and checked before and after scenario/flow actions where applicable. Direct reads of a missing instance make an invariant inapplicable to that snapshot. Quantified reads follow present scope members. Keep one-field constraints in Field; use invariants for relationships between fields or entities.

docs.title: Action and effects
docs.text:
Action(pre=[...], effect=[...], post=[...], emits=[...]) declares a transition. Metadata includes id, name, description and tags.

from analint import Action, Set, Subtract

pay = Action(
    pre=[Wallet.balance >= Order.total],
    effect=[
        Subtract(Wallet.balance, Order.total),
        Set(Order.paid, True),
    ],
    post=[Order.paid],
)
Effect Meaning Set(field, value_or_expression) The field has this value in the next state Add(field, amount) / Subtract(field, amount) Arithmetic forms of Set Create(ref, **fields) An absent scoped slot becomes present; omitted fields take defaults Delete(ref) A present scoped slot becomes absent

Effects are simultaneous: every right-hand side reads the pre-state, so list order cannot express a sequence. Two writes to one field are invalid. A slot cannot be created/deleted and also written by another effect in the same action. Use multiple actions in a flow when intermediate states matter.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Declare a lifecycle inline as a field default:

from analint import Lifecycle

status: Status = Lifecycle(
    initial=Status.NEW,
    transitions={
        Status.NEW: [Status.RESOLVED],
        Status.RESOLVED: [Status.ARCHIVED],
    },
    terminal=[Status.ARCHIVED],
)

Effects that change the field must follow a declared edge. terminal freezes the whole entity, including its other fields and deletion. Missing outgoing edges do not implicitly declare a terminal state. A declared edge out of a terminal state is a structural error.

docs.title: Scope, presence and instance references
docs.text:
A Scope(EntityClass, keys=[...]) allocates a fixed finite universe. Indexing returns an InstanceRef; ref.field addresses a particular instance and ref(field=value) creates its snapshot.

from analint import Absent, Present, Scope

wallets = Scope(Wallet, keys=["alice", "bob"])
alice = wallets["alice"]
bob = wallets["bob"]

alice_has_funds = alice.balance > 0
alice_exists = Present(alice)
# Snapshot entries: alice(balance=3), Absent(bob)

Use instance fields rather than ambiguous Wallet.balance once Wallet is scoped. Only one scope per entity type is supported. Absent(ref) marks a slot absent; Present(ref_or_bound_or_param) tests membership. Scenarios/flows omit slots as absent, while exploration defaults them to present unless overridden.

Ordinary field reads and writes need a present slot. Create requires absence, Delete requires presence; a mismatch rejects the action before effects. Keys never grow dynamically. Guard a possibly absent field read with And(Present(ref), ref.field == value) so absence does not cause an evaluation error.

docs.title: Declared keys and initial presence
docs.text:
The following APIs are available since 0.0.4.

Key(ref_or_param_or_bound) is a value expression returning the slot's declared key, with its original type. It accepts an InstanceRef, a Param whose entire domain consists of instance references, or a quantified Bound. Values may be None, booleans, integers, finite floats, strings or Enum members. Other hashable scope keys remain supported as identities but cannot be used with Key. Identity is independent of presence: Key(ref) works for an absent slot and reads no state. A Bound needs an enclosing quantifier/aggregate; an instance Param is substituted during action expansion. Static Action.where filters can compare keys. There is no automatic conversion between a scope key and a foreign-key field: use the same domain values, such as Enum members, in both.

Scope(..., initially_present=False) makes omitted slots absent when building canonical and query roots. The default is True, preserving existing models. Explicit ref(...) and Absent(ref) snapshots override the policy. Each query-owned given, given_any world or Initial is built independently from the scope defaults and its own snapshots; it does not merge canonical snapshots. Queries without their own source inherit the canonical worlds. Scenarios and flows continue to treat omitted slots as absent regardless of this policy. Varying a field of an absent slot remains an error; supply a present snapshot before including that field in Initial.vary.

This complete example starts with an empty scope, then records an absent slot's identity as the owner of a created slot:

scope-identity-spec.py
from analint import (
    Absent, Action, And, Bound, Create, Delete, Entity, ForAll, In,
    Invariant, Key, Not, Present, Reachable, Scenario, Scope, Spec,
)


class Item(Entity):
    owner: str = "none"


slots = Scope(Item, keys=["a", "b"], initially_present=False)
a, b = slots["a"], slots["b"]
x = Bound("x", slots)

create = Action(effect=[Create(b, owner=Key(a))])
delete = Action(effect=[Delete(b)])
safe = Invariant(ForAll(x, In(x.owner, ["none", Key(a)])))
query = Reachable(And(Present(b), b.owner == Key(a)))

created = Scenario(
    name="Create with the declared owner", action=create, given=[Absent(b)],
    then=[Present(b), b.owner == "a"],
)
deleted = Scenario(
    name="Delete an owned slot", action=delete, given=[b(owner="a")],
    then=[Not(Present(b))],
)

spec = Spec(
    id="scope-identity", name="Declared identity and empty initial scope",
    actions=[create, delete], invariants=[safe], queries=[query],
    scenarios=[created, deleted],
)

check proves the invariant and reaches the query through create; the complete graph contains two states. trace query shows Item['b'].owner becoming "a". The exploration/trace JSON schemas keep their existing scalar representation (Enum values use Type.MEMBER); model views add initially_present to scope metadata. TLC exports keys through its existing literal encoding. Unsupported values such as floating-point keys cause an explicit export refusal and leave the check INCONCLUSIVE; they are never approximated.

docs.title: Param: finite action families
docs.text:
Param(name, *domain) accepts explicit values, entity classes, enums, booleans or a scope. Param(name, ge=N, le=M) declares an inclusive integer range.

from analint import Action, Add, Param, Subtract

src = Param("src", wallets)
dst = Param("dst", wallets)

transfer = Action(
    params=[src, dst],
    where=[src != dst],
    pre=[src.balance >= 1, dst.balance < 5],
    effect=[Subtract(src.balance, 1), Add(dst.balance, 1)],
)

alice_pays_bob = transfer.bind(src=alice, dst=bob)

The declaration expands into ordinary bound actions when the Spec is built. where filters static parameter combinations; state-dependent conditions, including Present, belong in pre. List the family on Spec.actions, and use .bind(...) to select the concrete action for a scenario or flow. Do not generate model elements with Python factory loops; finite families belong in Param.

docs.title: Bound, quantifiers and aggregates
docs.text:
Bound(name, scope) binds a variable over present instances of that scope.

from analint import Bound, Count, Exists, ForAll, Max, Min, Sum

wallet = Bound("wallet", wallets)
all_nonnegative = ForAll(wallet, wallet.balance >= 0)
someone_has_funds = Exists(wallet, wallet.balance > 0)
funded_count = Count(wallet, wallet.balance > 0)
total_balance = Sum(wallet, wallet.balance)

ForAll and Exists are predicates. Count, Sum, Min and Max are arithmetic expressions usable in comparisons or effect right-hand sides. A bound field must occur within its quantifier/aggregate, or in the supported Initial.vary position.

Empty present set Result ForAll True Exists False Count, Sum 0 Min, Max Evaluation error

docs.title: Initial
docs.text:
Initial(vary=[...], where=[...], given=[...], max_candidates=10000) enumerates admissible roots. given fixes values, and where filters combinations with ordinary predicates and aggregates.

Since 0.0.4: vary can be omitted or empty. Initial(given=[...]) starts with one candidate built from defaults plus the supplied snapshots, then applies where. Initial() uses the defaults alone. A rejected candidate leaves no roots and fails validation; an evaluation error also fails. Versions before 0.0.4 require at least one varying field.

from analint import Initial

starting_balances = Initial(
    vary=[alice.balance],
    where=[alice.balance >= 1],
    given=[bob(balance=0)],
)

Attach it to Spec.initial for canonical verification or to a query's initial for that query only. Candidate overflow and evaluation errors fail rather than silently removing combinations. See initial states.

docs.title: Fixed-root example
docs.text:
Save this complete source as spec.py with analint 0.0.4 or newer installed and run analint check .. Both slots start absent; creating one increments the counter. The required Limit value comes from given. An independent noise action shows why property slices can be smaller than analint explore .'s whole-model graph. already_created supplies its own fixed root and needs no action to find a witness.

fixed-root-spec.py
from analint import (
    Absent, Action, Add, Bound, Create, Entity, Field, Initial,
    Invariant, Not, Present, Reachable, Scenario, Scope, Set, Spec, Sum,
)


class Limit(Entity):
    max_created: int


class Counter(Entity):
    n: int = Field(0, ge=0, le=1)


class Item(Entity):
    units: int = Field(1, ge=1, le=1)


class Noise(Entity):
    on: bool = False


items = Scope(Item, keys=["one", "spare"])
one = items["one"]
spare = items["spare"]
item = Bound("item", items)

create = Action(
    pre=[Counter.n < Limit.max_created],
    effect=[Create(one), Add(Counter.n, 1)],
)
flip_noise = Action(pre=[Not(Noise.on)], effect=[Set(Noise.on, True)])
balanced = Invariant(Sum(item, item.units) == Counter.n)
created = Reachable(Present(one))
already_created = Reachable(
    Present(one),
    initial=Initial(given=[Limit(max_created=1), Counter(n=1), one(), Absent(spare)]),
)
create_once = Scenario(
    action=create,
    given=[Limit(max_created=1), Counter(), Absent(one), Absent(spare)],
    then=[Present(one), Counter.n == 1],
)
noise_once = Scenario(action=flip_noise, given=[Noise()], then=[Noise.on])

spec = Spec(
    id="fixed_initial",
    name="Fixed initial world",
    initial=Initial(given=[Limit(max_created=1), Absent(one), Absent(spare)]),
    actions=[create, flip_noise],
    scenarios=[create_once, noise_once],
    invariants=[balanced],
    queries=[created, already_created],
)

The canonical whole-model graph has one root and four states; the invariant and created each need only two states in their slices. Use analint trace created with -p . for the create witness, or analint trace already_created -p . for the query-specific initial-state witness.

docs.title: Event and Emitted
docs.text:
Event uses typed fields like Entity. Action.emits accepts an event class or a payload template whose fields bind to state expressions:

from analint import Emitted, Event


class PaymentRecorded(Event):
    amount: int


# On an action: emits=[PaymentRecorded(amount=Order.total)]
# In Scenario.then or Flow.steps: Emitted(PaymentRecorded)

Payload templates are type-checked and materialized against the post-state. Emission does not dispatch another action. A scenario can supply an Event instance in given to test an action with payload preconditions; such external inputs are not generated by reachability exploration. They are reported as unassessed.

docs.title: Scenario and Flow
docs.text:
Scenario(action=..., given=[...], then=[...], expected=Expect.PASS) checks one action. then accepts predicates and Emitted checks. Expect.FAIL expects pre-execution rejection, not a runtime defect.

Flow(given=[...], steps=[...]) executes a journey. Steps mix actions with Assert(predicate) and Emitted(EventClass) checkpoints. given is required; given=[] starts with an empty world. Only present instances are available, and each accepted step's state feeds the next step. A rejection or defect fails the flow. Both declarations accept ids and descriptive metadata; the tutorial shows complete examples.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
Declaration Requirement Reachable(predicate) A matching state can be reached from each root Unreachable(predicate) No matching state can be reached AlwaysHolds(predicate) The predicate holds in every applicable reachable state NoDeadEnd(goal=predicate) A goal state remains reachable from every reachable state DeadActions() Assess which actions can never fire in the explored model

Each accepts id, label, max_states and one optional initial source: given, given_any or initial. Queries with none inherit the canonical roots. NoDeadEnd is recoverability, not a guarantee that every execution terminates. Excluded event-input actions are unassessed, not dead.

docs.title: Spec, Contract and loading
docs.text:
Spec(id=..., name=..., actions=[...], invariants=[...], scenarios=[...], flows=[...], queries=[...]) is the root. It can additionally list entities, events, scopes and lifecycles, which are otherwise derived from referenced behaviour. Spec.initial supplies canonical roots; Spec.max_states sets the canonical exploration budget (default 10,000).

Contract(id=..., actions=[...], ...) is an explicit reusable fragment with the same content lists. Spec(imports=[contract, ...], ...) combines those lists with the root's own. Contract version is descriptive metadata, not a resolver that downloads dependencies.

Load one entry point: a spec.py directory or an explicit Python file. Multi-file models should be packages with __init__.py and relative imports. List behaviour explicitly: merely importing a file does not register its actions or properties. The loader names empty ids from variable names, warns about unlisted behaviour and unreachable files, and rejects multiple Spec roots in one import graph. An empty behaviour model is an error.

The taskboard and broker examples show composition. Use analint show contract ID -p PATH to inspect a contract's public surface.

docs.title: Examples gallery
docs.text:
Clone the repository to run these models; the Python package installation does not place the examples in your working directory:

git clone https://github.com/angru/analint
cd analint
uv sync --frozen
uv run analint check examples/cloak/

Each example has a README describing its assumptions and intended result. examples/expectations.toml records verdicts separately from the detailed regression snapshots. A deliberately failing model is a successful demonstration when it exposes the documented defect.

docs.title: Scaling benchmarks
docs.text:
benchmarks/broker/m4.py, m5.py and m6.py extend the broker baseline with risk, partner restrictions and bounded multiplicity. They are experimental benchmark entries, separate from the example-intent gallery. Their composed explorations can exhaust their budget and remain INCONCLUSIVE; executable fixture scenarios do not replace a complete canonical proof. See the broker benchmark notes for bounds, measurements and the separate settlement abstractions.

The verification concepts explain how to distinguish a counterexample, an expected rejection and an unfinished exploration.

docs.title: Your first spec
docs.text: This example models one support ticket and a queue counter. Resolving the ticket must decrement the counter; only a resolved ticket can be archived. The finite model has three reachable states.

docs.title: Install and declare the model
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12 or newer:

pip install analint
mkdir ticket_spec
cd ticket_spec

Save the complete program below as spec.py. The documentation checks execute this exact block, including the defect exercise later on this page.

spec.py
from enum import StrEnum

from analint import (
    Action, Assert, Entity, Expect, Field, Flow, Implies, Invariant,
    Lifecycle, NoDeadEnd, Reachable, Scenario, Set, Spec, Subtract,
)


class Status(StrEnum):
    NEW = "new"
    RESOLVED = "resolved"
    ARCHIVED = "archived"


class Ticket(Entity):
    status: Status = Lifecycle(
        initial=Status.NEW,
        transitions={
            Status.NEW: [Status.RESOLVED],
            Status.RESOLVED: [Status.ARCHIVED],
        },
        terminal=[Status.ARCHIVED],
    )


class Queue(Entity):
    open_tickets: int = Field(1, ge=0, le=1)


resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket = Invariant(
    Implies(Ticket.status != Status.NEW, Queue.open_tickets == 0),
    label="Resolving the only ticket clears the queue counter",
)

resolve = Action(
    pre=[Ticket.status == Status.NEW],
    effect=[
        Set(Ticket.status, Status.RESOLVED),
        Subtract(Queue.open_tickets, 1),
    ],
)

archive = Action(
    pre=[Ticket.status == Status.RESOLVED],
    effect=[Set(Ticket.status, Status.ARCHIVED)],
)

resolve_new = Scenario(
    action=resolve,
    given=[Ticket(), Queue()],
    then=[Ticket.status == Status.RESOLVED, Queue.open_tickets == 0],
)

cannot_archive_new = Scenario(
    action=archive,
    given=[Ticket(), Queue()],
    expected=Expect.FAIL,
)

ticket_journey = Flow(
    given=[Ticket(), Queue()],
    steps=[
        resolve,
        Assert(Queue.open_tickets == 0),
        archive,
        Assert(Ticket.status == Status.ARCHIVED),
    ],
)

can_archive = Reachable(Ticket.status == Status.ARCHIVED)
archive_stays_possible = NoDeadEnd(goal=Ticket.status == Status.ARCHIVED)

spec = Spec(
    id="tickets",
    name="Ticket workflow",
    actions=[resolve, archive],
    invariants=[resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket],
    scenarios=[resolve_new, cannot_archive_new],
    flows=[ticket_journey],
    queries=[can_archive, archive_stays_possible],
)

The model contains the behaviour explicitly listed on Spec. Its entity types and inline lifecycle are derived from those references. Variable names supply ids such as resolve and can_archive; defining another action without listing it does not add it to the model.

docs.title: Run and interpret the checks
docs.text:
analint check .
analint check . --format json

Both scenarios, the flow, the invariant and both queries pass. The overall JSON has schema: "analint.check/v1", verdict: "PASS" and passed: true; the command exits with code 0.

cannot_archive_new passes because the archive precondition rejects a new ticket before execution. Expect.FAIL checks an intended rejection; it does not excuse a broken effect, postcondition or assertion.

The scenario and flow start from their own given snapshots. Reachability and automatic invariant verification use the canonical model, which here starts from the field defaults: a new ticket and one open ticket. Exploration checks every enabled action order within that model.

docs.title: Inspect before editing
docs.text:
analint show -p .
analint show action resolve -p .
analint affects Queue.open_tickets -p .
analint trace can_archive -p .

show and affects return JSON. The trace reaches the archived state through resolve → archive, showing the counter and status changes. NoDeadEnd says archiving remains possible from every reachable state; it makes no scheduling promise that a user will actually perform those actions.

docs.title: Introduce a defect
docs.text:
Delete this one effect from resolve:

Subtract(Queue.open_tickets, 1),

Run the check again:

analint check .
analint trace resolved_leaves_no_open_ticket -p . --format json

The check now fails with exit code 1. The counterexample reaches a resolved ticket with Queue.open_tickets still equal to 1. The invariant trace names the property under its invariant key and shows resolve as the violating step. The invariant-invalid state is retained as evidence and has no outgoing transitions. Restore the removed effect and check that the model passes again.

docs.title: Test a proposed rule without changing the model
docs.text:
First make the spec a Python package so that the checker and hypothesis share the same entity classes. From inside ticket_spec, create an empty __init__.py, then return to its parent directory:

touch __init__.py
cd ..

Save this separate file as hypothesis.py alongside the ticket_spec directory:

hypothesis.py
from analint import Invariant
from ticket_spec.spec import Queue

queue_is_always_empty = Invariant(Queue.open_tickets == 0)

Then check it against the restored model:

analint check ticket_spec --what-if hypothesis.py
analint trace queue_is_always_empty -p ticket_spec --what-if hypothesis.py

This hypothesis fails at the initial state: the new ticket is still open. The extra module is merged for this run; spec.py is unchanged. Scratch files outside the spec directory do not cause unloaded-file warnings on normal checks. Import shared types by their package name; importing a standalone entry as a second module can create different entity identities.

Next, read verification concepts for roots, budgets and slicing, or the DSL reference to model multiple tickets with a Scope.
